subject: Hosted API volume & peak TPS — pricing confirmation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Morales <lauren.morales@shopwise.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API volume & peak TPS — pricing confirmation

Hi Lauren — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and a few questions so we can produce a tailored hosted-API pricing scenario for ShopWise.

Summary from the call:
- Primary product: conversational customer support assistant + daily analytics jobs that produce batched embeddings.
- Expected steady-state: a mix of short chat turns and background embedding jobs.
- Key ask: target unit economics and monthly budget range to evaluate fits between our hosted tiers.

What we need to confirm (one-line answers are perfect):
1) Expected total tokens per calendar month (approx). For budgeting we usually model in 1M-token increments.
2) Peak sustained TPS (requests per second) during busy windows — e.g., support spikes or promotional events.
3) Typical token split: what % of tokens are chat (many short turns) vs bulk embeddings/rerank.
4) Target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range you are looking to hit.

From our side, initial scenarios to consider once we have numbers:
- 50M tokens/mo, peak 5 TPS -> hosted standard tier estimate (with basic batching/caching).
- 200M tokens/mo, peak 12 TPS -> may benefit from dedicated reserved capacity for cost predictability.

I attached a quick pricing model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx) with example $/1M assumptions; we can walk through it on a short follow-up if that helps.

Next step: if you can reply with the three bullets above, Priya and I will run the unit-economics and propose 2 pricing scenarios (hosted and small dedicated). Hoping to align on budget range so we can include any committed throughput assumptions.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Lauren Morales <lauren.morales@shopwise.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted API volume & peak TPS — pricing confirmation

Thanks Sean — quick answers below based on our internal planning and the pilot cohort we expect to run in Q2.

1) Expected total tokens/month: ~50,000,000 tokens (we expect initial months 30–60M, ramp to ~100M over 6 months if pilot succeeds).
2) Peak sustained TPS: roughly 6–8 TPS during business hours; during promotional blasts we could see short spikes up to ~12 TPS for several minutes.
3) Token split: approximately 70% chat (short turns, avg 60–120 tokens per request), 30% embeddings/batch jobs (large batched jobs run nightly).
4) Budget range: currently evaluating $3,000–$6,000/month for hosted inference. If unit economics/baselines look favorable we could consider committed spend. Target cost target is roughly $50–$60 / 1M tokens as an internal benchmark to compare vendors, but flexibility exists if caching/batching substantially reduces effective cost.

Let me know if you need different granularity (e.g., tokens per chat-request or estimated embedding batch sizes). Happy to hop on a 30-min call.

—Lauren Morales
Director, Product Operations | ShopWise
lauren.morales@shopwise.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Morales <lauren.morales@shopwise.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API volume & peak TPS — pricing confirmation

Lauren — perfect, thanks for the clear numbers. A few follow-ups and what we’ll deliver next:

Follow-ups:
- Can you confirm average tokens per chat request (you mentioned 60–120; a single number or a 60/120 split helps).
- For embedding batches: how large is a nightly job (e.g., total docs processed or tokens per batch)?

What we’ll run and return by EOD Thu:
- Two hosted scenarios using your $3k–$6k budget: conservative (no committed discount) and committed (1–3 month commit) with estimated $/1M tokens and projected out-of-pocket monthly.
- A quick sensitivity table showing how KV/prefix caching and batching affects effective $/1M tokens for chat-heavy vs embedding-heavy workloads.
- A recommended peak TPS plan and whether a short-term burst option is needed during promotions.

I’ve attached a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.docx) that lays out milestones and timelines if you want to move forward after pricing. If the $50–$60 / 1M token benchmark is the bar, we’ll show you where hosting without commitments sits and what level of commit or minor architecture changes (more aggressive caching, client-side length controls) would be required to approach $40 / 1M.

Would you be available Thu 11am PT for a 30-min review? If so we’ll include Marissa (SRE/solutions) to confirm the peak TPS behavior and Dev for any perf questions.

Best — Sean

Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx (document stub)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Morales <lauren.morales@shopwise.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API volume & peak TPS — pricing confirmation

Hi Lauren — looping in Marissa (solutions) and Dev (SE) to make the Thu 11am PT call efficient. A couple quick technical clarifications ahead of the call so we can prepare:

- For chat token averages: if you can confirm a mean token/turn (e.g., 85 tokens) that helps our cost model—otherwise we’ll use 90 as a working assumption.
- For embedding batches: please share an example batch size (number of docs) or an estimated token count for the nightly job. If the batches are >10M tokens we’ll treat them as a separate cost center for batching/discount modeling.
- Are there any compliance constraints (data residency or retention) that would push you towards dedicated/private options?

We’ll prepare two concrete hosted pricing scenarios (no commit vs 3-month commit) and a short note on when Dedicated becomes the better economic choice given higher sustained volume/peak TPS. Expect the deck and numbers in your inbox by Thu morning.

Thanks — Priya
Account Strategist | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
